column1: # The acceptance-criterion exemptions (E11, out of the register sweep of 2026-09-15).
# EPICS.md states acceptance criteria as check boxes; TASKS.md states register rows as statuses.
# Where a criterion cites EXACTLY ONE row, the two are claims about the same thing, and
# AcceptanceCriterionChecks asserts they agree: the box is ticked if and only if the row is Done.
# 154 criteria cite exactly one row. 22 disagreed when the check was written; 17 were the documents
# lagging the work and were ticked, and the five below are the ones where disagreeing is correct.
# A CRITERION IS NOT ITS ROW. That is the whole reason this file exists. A criterion may be a part
# of a row, so it is met while the row is not; or broader than the row, so the row is Done and the
# criterion is not. Either way the reason is written here rather than hidden in the predicate, and
# a reason that stops being true fails the check: an exemption whose row and box now agree is a
# STALE exemption and is reported, so this file cannot become the place fixed problems go to be
# forgotten.
# KEYED ON THE CRITERION, NOT ON THE ROW, because a row can be cited by several criteria and they
# do not all need excusing - E2-T28 is cited by three and exactly one of them is here. Match must
# select exactly one criterion citing Row, or the check fails rather than guessing.
# Row       the register row the criterion cites.
# Expect    the state the box is expected to be in: Ticked or Unticked.
# Match     a distinctive substring of the criterion, which must select exactly one of them.
# Reason    why, in a sentence a stranger can check.
